Definition: prolongation from πέρθω (to sack); to ravage (figuratively):--destroy, waste.
BiblicalUsage: Portheo means to ravage, to destroy, to waste, and Paul uses it for his own past. The churches heard that he who once destroyed them now preaches the faith he once destroyed, and Paul himself says he persecuted the church of God and wasted it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the destroyer turned preacher is the gospel in one life, and no past is too violent for grace to reverse.
